chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who shortens his prayer in his country estate. He said: 'There is no harm [in shortening] as long as he does not intend to stay for ten days, unless he has a house in it that he makes his permanent residence.' I said: 'What is making it a permanent residence?' He said: 'That he has a house in it in which he stays for six months. If that is the case, he completes his prayer in it whenever he enters it.'.

And he said: And Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed me that he prayed in his country estate and shortened his prayer. Ahmad said: And Ali ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd and Ahmad ibn Muhammad both informed me that his country estate where he shortened [his prayer] was Al-Hamra'.
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler need to pray full prayers instead of shortened prayers when staying in a country estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary travel and permanent settlement (*istitan*) in rural estates (*day'a*), establishing that shortening prayer (*qasr*) remains valid unless one intends a ten-day stay or maintains a home for six months. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) and physical continuity of residence as key determinants for changing prayer status, ensuring that travelers do not prematurely assume the obligations of a resident (*muqim*).
